page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96-lssd is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz, this x86_64 architecture includes 504 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for vector and matrix operations. The instance is configured with 360 GB of system memory, yielding 3.75 GB per core, and integrates 16 local NVMe SSDs providing 6,167 GB of direct-attached storage. No GPU resources are included.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the top tier for several compute and memory-intensive tasks. It achieves a Passmark CPU score of 110,513.48 and demonstrates top-tier performance in database operations and Redis SET operations, reaching 171.76 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, with cached small-block reads peaking at 7,717.61 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 356.38 GB/sec. Multi-threaded decompression via bzip3 also registers in the top tier at 636.02 GB/sec.

While multi-core performance and vector-heavy workloads excel due to the dedicated Intel Xeon architecture, single-core CPU performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core metrics falling into the average category. Similarly, while LLM prompt processing speeds are strong to top-tier, text generation speeds drop to average levels, such as 4.54 tokens/sec for a 70B model. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated compute cores combined with massive local NVMe storage reduces the need for external block storage, making it resource-efficient for I/O-heavy workloads, though the lack of GPU acceleration limits its utility for large-scale deep learning training.

This configuration is suited for high-throughput database hosting, large-scale software compilation, real-time data processing, and static web serving. The combination of high-speed local NVMe storage and Intel AMX instructions also supports CPU-based machine learning inference and cryptography-heavy applications.
